issues.legal_issue: A class bequest to descendants is limited to the class members alive at the testator’s death when their possession is not postponed beyond that death.
material_facts: The testator’s will devised his estate in equal shares to his grandsons then alive and to any further male children of his son who might be born later, with the beneficiaries to take and enjoy the property after the testator’s death.
The will appointed the beneficiaries’ parents as guardians and executors to manage the property for the minors and deliver it when they attained majority.
The will did not make a prior bequest or reserve legal possession for another person.
Two additional grandsons were born after the testator’s death; the tax authorities assessed the two grandsons alive at the testator’s death on equal shares of the estate’s income.
issues.conclusion: The two grandsons alive at the testator’s death alone took the estate in equal shares, and the assessments of their shares of its income were valid; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 111 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, a bequest to a class ordinarily goes to those class members alive at the testator’s death. The exception applies where the class is described by its relationship to a specified individual and possession is deferred beyond the testator’s death: those in the class at the deferred date, and representatives of class members who died after the testator, take. Here the beneficiaries’ parents’ management of the property as guardians did not defer legal possession. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: income_tax_assessment_dispute and class_bequest and class_described_by_relationship and possession_not_deferred and no_intervening_possession_right

predicates.income_tax_assessment_dispute: The dispute concerns whether income from an estate was properly assessed against the beneficiaries of a will.
predicates.class_bequest: The testator gave the property to beneficiaries described as members of a class.
predicates.class_described_by_relationship: The will defined the class by the beneficiaries’ relationship to a specified individual.
predicates.possession_not_deferred: The testator directed that the beneficiaries take the property after his death, without postponing their legal possession to a later time.
predicates.no_intervening_possession_right: The testator did not give or reserve legal possession of the property to another person before the beneficiaries took it.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment dispute concerns a relationship-defined class bequest whose legal possession is not postponed and is not given or reserved to someone else, the assessment against class members alive at the testator’s death is valid.
